pages.text: The Dragon Head commonly found in End Cities can be altered into a False Bloodwyrm Head. This change is primarily visual and offers no specific benefits. To unlock its offensive potential, it has to be combined with a Blood Feather and an Organic Matter in a Smithing Table, transforming it into a False Bloodwyrm Spewer.

The Spewer can spread fire in front of the wielder and can be refueled with Dragon Breath. Additionally, the spray will also inflict the Flame Frailty effect onto the victim, making them considerably more susceptible to fire.

pages.title: Addendum
pages.text: The False Bloodwyrm Head causes me so much frustration. I came across it whenever I was testing item alterations and at first, I was confused on why the alteration of a Dragon Head seemed so... lackluster. Then I learned, after consulting some literature on the topic, that Bloodwyrms are a type of Offspring that can be found in the world, though stupidly rarely. The documentation on them is extremely scarce, with most

only detailing how their level of danger rivals the one posed by Seraphims - if it doesn't straight up exceed it. Now with the False Bloodwyrm Head, it eludes to the idea that the Ender Dragon and the Bloodwyrm have some sort of shared origin but that also a Bloodwyrm isn't just a 'Risus Ender Dragon'. There must be an additional element or power that allows the creation of a True Bloodwyrm from a false one... Yet, I've been unable to find it. At this point, I think the only way to resolve this
mystery is to actually find a Bloodwyrm - and I have no leads on how I would do that. That's why it's so frustrating...
